nodes.summary: For an instance $(n, E)$, the graph of the instance is the simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent exactly when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $E$. Pairs in $E$ with an entry at least $n$, and pairs $(u, u)$, contribute no edge.
nodes.title: Graph of a PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of instances, to an instance $(n, E)$ that is well formed and admits a partition into paths of length 2. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ admits a partition into paths of length 2 when there is a list of triples, each a list of three distinct vertices from $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, such that every vertex occurs exactly once among all the triples taken together, and every triple contains pairwise distinct vertices $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $x$ is adjacent to $y$ and $y$ is adjacent to $z$ in the graph of the instance.
nodes.title: Partitions into paths of length 2

nodes.summary: An instance of PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 is a pair $(n, E)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a finite list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edge list.
nodes.title: Instances of PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2

nodes.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and the reversed pair $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed PARTITION INTO PATHS OF LENGTH 2 instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
